title: Topology-driven steady-state simulator for mixed-tokenflow batching and queueing effects
creator: Marco Chen
description: Goal: Build a topology-driven steady-state simulator to measure how continuous batching and queueing interact under mixed tokenflow workloads and to produce robust p95/tokens-per-second surfaces and automatic regression signals. Motivation: existing burst-oriented probes miss long-tail amplification that emerges when many tenants with heterogeneous session lengths share batching queues and prefix/KV caches. Approach: synthesize tenant topologies (session length distribution, request arrival clustering, KV prefix locality) and run long steady-state experiments (1–6 hours) that record per-model, per-route, per-tenant p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec. Novelty: instead of replaying single-trace mixes, the harness composes small probabilistic topologies and enforces a topology affinity graph so we can probe topology-level coupling (e.g., large-session-heavy tenants colocated with many small-session clients). The simulator supports deterministic seeds, cold/warm cache phases, and hooks for injecting transient capacity constraints and routing fallbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Produces repeatable steady-state runs (seeded) with >90% result stability across 3 runs for p50/p95 at target load
Generates a 2D heatmap (utilization vs mix skew) of p95 and tokens/sec for each model variant and autoscaling policy
Implements automatic regression detection based on baseline divergence with configurable thresholds and alerts (email/Slack/Grafana)
Includes KV-prefix warmup and cold-start experiments with measured impact on tokens/sec and tail latency
Deliver a public dashboard and an artifact bundle (CSV + annotated run metadata) for every experiment
implementation_notes: Harness architecture: controller (Go) schedules synthetic tenants -> worker pools simulate client sessions -> runtime test harnesses (Dockerized) call inference endpoints and emit OpenTelemetry traces
Workload generator: parameterized distributions for session length, inter-arrival (Weibull/Poisson mixture), token length distribution, and preference for prefix reuse
Telemetry: tag traces with topology_id, tenant_class, model_variant, route, batch_size, queue_depth, kv_cache_state
Determinism: seed RNG for session generation and request timing; log seeds in run metadata for reproducibility
Cost: long steady-state runs increase infra cost; include fast-mode sampling (30m) and full-mode (4h)

tradeoffs: Synthetic topology gives better coverage of corner cases but may miss real-world correlated arrival modes present in production traces
Long steady-state runs are required to observe amplification but increase infra and experiment time; we provide sampled short runs for quick iteration
Prefetching KV reduces cold-tail but can mask cache-miss interactions that matter for real cold-start customer behavior
observed_findings: Nonlinear p95 amplification observed when utilization crosses 60-70% under skewed mixes; amplification correlates with increased average batch size variance and queueing depth
KV-prefix cold sessions cause a transient tokens/sec drop up to 30% for small-batch clients; adding a short prefill phase mitigates most of the drop
Autoscaler cooldown interactions can create oscillations that worsen tail latency when combined with continuous batching because small downward scale events increase queueing transiently
Regression detection baseline must consider topology drift; a simple global p95 delta produced many false positives during topology composition changes
